runbook: R-18 / R-19 (fresh independent oracle; evidence tree = git archive HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md only)
old_value: Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input; item presence alone never assumes stasis.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

item_identification.how: The leaf's reason text names the behavior 'Time Stop'. Grepping the export for that string resolves it to exactly two cached items.
item_identification.note: Both declare the identical family set (stats + crowd-control-mobility + damage), so every finding below holds for either. Zhonya's Hourglass (3250g, tier 3, 'classic sr 5v5': true, shop tag MAGE) is the Summoner's Rift build item and is treated as the referent.

step_1_read_the_declared_families.finding: The new value's premise -- 'Every declared family on this item is a defence' -- is false on its face. The item declares the `damage` family (damage.resistance-mitigation, whose own relations point at damage-instance / armor-penetration / magic-penetration) and the `stats` family carrying 105 flat ability power.

step_2_no_defence_family_exists.method: Enumerated `family` over every file in data/item-atoms/*.json (1775 atoms).
step_2_no_defence_family_exists.schema_enum: data/atoms/atoms.schema.json family enum = [damage, heal, shield, crowd_control, stack, transform, summon, execute, resource, movement, vision, buff, debuff, interaction, economy]
step_2_no_defence_family_exists.finding: There is no 'defence' family in either taxonomy. The claim 'every declared family on this item is a defence' is not a statement that can be true of ANY cached item, let alone this one.

step_3_the_item_does_change_outgoing_TDD.finding: Holding the item changes outgoing TDD by roughly 150-365 damage on a single Syndra rotation. 'Changes durability, not outgoing TDD' is quantitatively false for this item.

step_4_the_active_is_conditional_and_bou.cached_wiki_text: Put yourself in {{tip|stasis (buff)|stasis}} for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, rendering you {{tip|untargetable}} and {{tip|invulnerable}} for the duration but also unable to move, declare [[basic attack]]s, cast [[champion ability|abilities]], use [[summoner spell]]s, or [[active ability items|activate items]].
findings: Time Stop is an ACTIVE ('Put yourself in stasis'), not a passive aura. Owning the item does not place the champion in stasis; a cast must occur. So 'item presence alone never assumes stasis' is exactly right.

Its duration is hard-bounded at 2.5 seconds by the same wiki line, which is what 'bounded active-seconds' names. Any pricing therefore needs the seconds as an explicit scenario input -- there is no defensible default.

Stasis is NOT TDD-neutral even in the charitable reading. The same sentence says the holder is 'unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items'. Over a fixed fight window the 2.5s is a dead window that REMOVES outgoing damage (e.g. ~0.36 of a 7s-cooldown Dark Sphere cast). A mechanic that subtracts damage output cannot be described as one that 'changes durability, not outgoing TDD'.

The signed direction of that effect is precisely why the value must come from the scenario input rather than from item presence: assuming stasis by default would silently deduct a rotation's worth of damage from every build containing the item.

quotes: "shield ... is pure mitigation and deliberately not modeled" (defensive, outside TDD scope)
"E passive damage reduction (defensive -- 'not modeled -- defensive only')"
step_5_convention_check.finding: A generic 'this is defensive, therefore out of TDD scope' reason is a real pattern in this corpus -- but it is applied to mechanics that are purely mitigation. Zhonya's Hourglass is not one of them: it is an offensive stat-stick (105 AP) carrying a conditional, castable, bounded, TDD-SUBTRACTING active. Applying the generic defensive-exclusion sentence to it misclassifies the item.

conclusion: The old value is a correct and precise statement about this item: Time Stop is an active with a 2.5s hard bound, so its cost/benefit is priced only from an explicitly supplied bounded active-seconds input, and mere possession of the item never implies stasis was entered. The new value is wrong on three independent counts: (a) the item's declared families are stats / crowd-control-mobility / damage, and no 'defence' family exists in either the item-atom taxonomy or atoms.schema.json, so 'every declared family is a defence' is unsatisfiable; (b) the item grants 105 AP, worth ~150-365 added TDD on one Syndra rotation, so it plainly does change outgoing damage; (c) even restricted to the active, stasis suppresses all actions for its duration, which changes outgoing TDD downward rather than leaving it untouched.
